{{nihongo|'''Asakura Shrine'''|旦椋神社 (宇治市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

'''Asakura Shrine''' (あさくらじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Okubo-chō Kitanoyama, {{ill|Uji|ar|يوجي (كيوتو)|azb|اوجی، کیوتو|bn|উজি, কিয়োটা|ca|Uji|ce|Удзи|cs|Udži (Kjóto)|de|Uji (Kyōto)|eo|Uĝi|es|Uji (Kioto)|et|Uji|eu|Uji (Kyoto)|fa|اوجی، کیوتو|fi|Uji|fr|Uji|gl|Uji|hr|Uji|hu|Udzsi|hy|Ուձի|id|Uji, Kyōto|it|Uji|ja|宇治市|ko|우지시|lt|Udžis|mg|Uji|mn|Үжи|ms|Uji, Kyoto|my|အုဂျိမြို့|mzn|اوجی، کیوتو|nl|Uji|no|Uji|pl|Uji (miasto)|pt|Uji|ro|Uji|ru|Удзи|sh|Uji|simple|Uji|sr|Уџи|sv|Uji, Kyōto|szl|Uji (mjasto)|tg|Уҷи|th|อูจิ|tl|Uji|tr|Uji|tt|Удзи|uk|Удзі (Кіото)|ur|اوجی|vi|Uji, Kyōto|war|Uji, Kyoto|zh|宇治市|zh_classical|宇治市|zh_min_nan|Uzi-chhī|zh_yue|宇治|qid=Q326956}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=minor Shikinaisha}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== History ===
The date of the shrine’s founding is unknown, but it is said that it was originally located in Okubo Asakura (west of the present site) in {{ill|Uji|ar|يوجي (كيوتو)|azb|اوجی، کیوتو|bn|উজি, কিয়োটা|ca|Uji|ce|Удзи|cs|Udži (Kjóto)|de|Uji (Kyōto)|eo|Uĝi|es|Uji (Kioto)|et|Uji|eu|Uji (Kyoto)|fa|اوجی، کیوتو|fi|Uji|fr|Uji|gl|Uji|hr|Uji|hu|Udzsi|hy|Ուձի|id|Uji, Kyōto|it|Uji|ja|宇治市|ko|우지시|lt|Udžis|mg|Uji|mn|Үжи|ms|Uji, Kyoto|my|အုဂျိမြို့|mzn|اوجی، کیوتو|nl|Uji|no|Uji|pl|Uji (miasto)|pt|Uji|ro|Uji|ru|Удзи|sh|Uji|simple|Uji|sr|Уџи|sv|Uji, Kyōto|szl|Uji (mjasto)|tg|Уҷи|th|อูจิ|tl|Uji|tr|Uji|tt|Удзи|uk|Удзі (Кіото)|ur|اوجی|vi|Uji, Kyōto|war|Uji, Kyoto|zh|宇治市|zh_classical|宇治市|zh_min_nan|Uzi-chhī|zh_yue|宇治|qid=Q326956}}. According to {{ill|Archaeological excavation|ar|حفريات (آثار)|ast|Escavación arqueolóxica|az|Arxeoloji qazıntı|be|Археалагічныя раскопкі|bg|Археологически разкопки|ca|Excavació arqueològica|cs|Archeologický výzkum|da|Udgravning|de|Ausgrabung|el|Ανασκαφή (αρχαιολογία)|es|Excavación|et|Arheoloogilised väljakaevamised|fa|کاوش باستان‌شناسی|fi|Kaivaus|fr|Fouille|fy|Archeologyske opgraving|he|חפירה ארכאולוגית|hi|उत्खनन (पुरातत्व)|hy|Հնագիտական պեղումներ|id|Penggalian (arkeologi)|is|Uppgröftur|it|Scavo (archeologia)|ja|発掘調査|kk|Археологиялық қазбалар|kn|ಉತ್ಖನನ|ko|발굴|lv|Arheoloģiskie izrakumi|mk|Археолошко ископување|mr|पुरातत्त्वीय उत्खनन|ms|Ekskavasi|nl|Archeologische opgraving|no|Utgravning|pl|Wykopaliska|ps|کیندنه (لرغونپوهنه)|pt|Escavação|ru|Раскопки|si|කැණීම|sv|Utgrävning|ta|அகழ்வாய்வு|tr|Arkeolojik kazı|uz|Arxeologik qazish|wa|Fougnaedje arkeyolodjike|zh|考古发掘|qid=Q959782}} of the former site, an earthen mound measuring 5.3 meters in length, 3.6 meters in width, and 50 centimeters in height remained in the middle of a rice field. Beneath the grass-covered topsoil, river stones approximately 20 centimeters in size were laid flat. Roof-tile fragments were excavated near the surface, leading to the supposition that a small shrine building once stood atop the stone pavement, probably facing south.

In {{ill|1550|Q6557|qid=Q6557}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tenbun}} 19), the shrine buildings were destroyed by fire, but in {{ill|1566|Q6638|qid=Q6638}} ({{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} 9), shrine buildings were rebuilt on the site of Tenman Tenjin, where rituals had been discontinued for more than 20 years, and Tenman Tenjin was enshrined together. After the reconstruction, it was revered as the village {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}} and was called Tenjinsha, Kurikuma Tenjinsha, or Kurikuma Tenmangū. In August {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6), it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}, and in June {{ill|1877|Q7773|qid=Q7773}} (Meiji 10), it was recognized as the Shikinaisha Asakurasha.
